title: Why Gratitude Is Good for Us

cards.answer: Lower stress and better sleep (also lower blood pressure, better relationships, etc.).

cards.prompt: In the journaling study, what did the gratitude group report?
cards.answer: They reported lower stress than the group recording irritations.

cards.prompt: Explain like I'm 10: why does gratitude make you want more of it?
cards.answer: Feeling grateful releases dopamine, which feels good, so you start looking for more things to be thankful for.

cards.prompt: You lie awake with racing worries. What did the study suggest?
cards.answer: Write a 15-minute journal before bed on what you were grateful for; it reduced intrusive thoughts and improved sleep.

cards.prompt: You can focus on positive and negative things equally at the same time.
cards.answer: Myth: we can't focus on both at the same time.

cards.prompt: Which is NOT a benefit of gratitude?
options: More gray matter in prefrontal cortex
